category: Style keys: shape, fill, stroke and text
description: Individual keys of the semicolon-separated mxCell style string that control shape geometry, fill, stroke and label text. Each entry documents one key (or a tightly related group), its values and defaults, so a program can compose or parse style strings exactly; the keys are set interactively through Edit > Edit Style (Ctrl+E) or the Format panel.

tools.name: shape (style key)
tools.description: Selects the renderer for a vertex or edge. Built-in vertex names include rectangle (default), ellipse, triangle, rhombus, hexagon, cylinder3, cloud, actor, process, note, card, document, parallelogram, trapezoid, step, tape, dataStorage, internalStorage, offPageConnector, singleArrow, doubleArrow, cross, corner, tee, plus, or, xor, umlActor, umlLifeline, umlFrame, umlDestroy, umlBoundary, umlEntity, umlControl, image, label, line, link, swimlane, table, tableRow, partialRectangle and mxgraph.<library>.<name> stencil ids. A style string without shape= renders a rectangle; several built-ins (ellipse, rhombus, triangle, hexagon, cylinder3, ...) may also be written as a bare first token.
tools.usage: shape=<name>;  (first token may also be the bare name, e.g. ellipse;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Built-in shape id or stencil id such as mxgraph.flowchart.decision, mxgraph.basic.rect, mxgraph.aws4.lambda_function, mxgraph.electrical.logic_gates.logic_gate.

parameters.name: stencil(...)
parameters.description: Inline custom shape: shape=stencil(<base64 of deflated shape XML>), produced by the Edit Shape dialog.

tools.notes: Many mxgraph.* stencils read extra keys (size, operation, direction, dx, dy) that the Format panel exposes under Property. To learn the exact string for any sidebar shape, drop it on the canvas and open Edit > Edit Style.

tools.name: rounded (style key)
tools.description: Enables rounded corners on rectangles, swimlanes, tables and many stencils, and rounded bends on orthogonal or elbow edges. Corner radius is controlled by arcSize; on edges it rounds each waypoint bend. Toggled with the Rounded checkbox in the Format panel Style tab.
tools.notes: For edges the bend radius is fixed by the renderer; arcSize applies to vertices only. curved=1 is an alternative for edges that draws smooth splines instead of rounded bends.

tools.name: arcSize (style key)
tools.description: Sets the corner radius used when rounded=1. By default it is a percentage of the shorter side (0-50, default 15 per cent of the shorter side); set absoluteArcSize=1 to interpret the value as pixels instead. The Format panel exposes it only through Edit Style.
tools.usage: arcSize=<number>;  (percent by default, pixels when absoluteArcSize=1)

parameters.name: arcSize
parameters.description: Radius as percentage of the shorter dimension (relative mode) or in pixels (absolute mode).

tools.notes: In relative mode an arcSize of 50 makes the short sides fully semicircular, which is how the sidebar's pill/rounded-rectangle button is built.

tools.name: absoluteArcSize (style key)
tools.description: Switches arcSize from a percentage of the shape's shorter side to an absolute pixel radius. Use it when a family of shapes of different sizes must share the same visible corner radius, for example UI mockups or cards.
tools.notes: Only meaningful together with rounded=1.

tools.name: whiteSpace (style key)
tools.description: Controls word wrapping of the label inside the vertex bounds. whiteSpace=wrap wraps long labels to the shape width (requires html=1); without it the label is a single line that may overflow. It corresponds to the Word Wrap checkbox in the Format panel Text tab and is part of the default vertex style created by the editor.

parameters.name: wrap
parameters.description: Wrap label text at the shape width.

parameters.name: nowrap
parameters.description: Single line, no wrapping (default when the key is absent).

tools.notes: Wrapping only works for HTML labels (html=1). Combine with overflow=hidden to clip text that still does not fit, or autosize=1 to grow the shape instead.

tools.name: html (style key)
tools.description: Marks the label as HTML so that rich formatting (bold, lists, line breaks, links, colours) is rendered and the in-place editor becomes a rich-text editor. Almost every style draw.io generates contains html=1; the Format panel calls it Formatted Text. Plain labels (html absent or 0) are rendered as SVG text and export more predictably.

parameters.description:
Label value is HTML; newlines must be written as
.

parameters.name: 0 or absent
parameters.description: Label is plain text; newlines in the value are honoured.

tools.notes: In the XML file HTML inside value must be entity-escaped. For SVG export, HTML labels are embedded as foreignObject, which some viewers cannot render; the export option Text settings > 'Embed images / convert text' or the configuration key foreignObjectImages addresses that.

tools.name: fillColor (style key)
tools.description: Background colour of a vertex (and of edge labels when labelBackgroundColor is not set). Accepts a hex colour, the keyword none for a transparent interior, or default to use the theme's shape background. The Format panel Fill colour control writes this key; gradientColor adds a second colour.

parameters.name: none
parameters.description: No fill; clicks pass through the interior unless pointerEvents=1.

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Theme background (white in light mode, dark grey in dark mode).

tools.notes: The built-in colour-scheme presets in the Style tab set fillColor, strokeColor and fontColor together. For swimlanes the header uses fillColor and the body uses swimlaneFillColor.

tools.name: gradientColor (style key)
tools.description: Second colour of a linear gradient that runs from fillColor to gradientColor. Set it to none to remove the gradient. The Format panel shows it as the Gradient checkbox and colour swatch next to Fill.
tools.notes: Gradients export to SVG and PNG; the PDF export rasterises complex gradients. Direction is set with gradientDirection.

tools.name: gradientDirection (style key)
tools.description: Orientation of the fillColor to gradientColor gradient. Values are the compass directions south (default, top to bottom), north, east and west; radial gradients are not supported by the core renderer.

parameters.name: south
parameters.description: fillColor at top, gradientColor at bottom (default).

parameters.name: east
parameters.description: fillColor on the left, gradientColor on the right.

tools.notes: Ignored when gradientColor is absent or none.

tools.name: fillOpacity (style key)
tools.description: Opacity of the fill only, from 0 (invisible) to 100 (opaque), independent of the stroke and text. Use it for translucent group boxes or overlays where the border and label must stay solid; the general opacity key affects the whole shape instead.
tools.notes: Related keys: strokeOpacity, textOpacity and opacity (all three together).

tools.name: strokeColor (style key)
tools.description: Colour of the outline of a vertex or the line of an edge. Accepts a hex colour, none (no border/line) or default (theme foreground). The Format panel's Line colour control writes this key; for edges it also colours the arrowheads.

parameters.name: none
parameters.description: No stroke; borderless text boxes use this together with fillColor=none.

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Theme foreground colour (black in light mode, light grey in dark mode).

tools.notes: Arrowheads use strokeColor for their outline and, when endFill=1, for their fill too.

tools.name: strokeWidth (style key)
tools.description: Line width in pixels for shape outlines and edges; decimals are allowed. The Format panel exposes it as the Line width spinner. Stencils declared with strokewidth="inherit" scale their internal lines with this value.
tools.notes: Arrowhead size scales with strokeWidth unless endSize/startSize are set explicitly.

tools.name: strokeOpacity (style key)
tools.description: Opacity of the outline or edge line only (0-100), leaving fill and text unaffected. Useful for faint guide lines or de-emphasised connectors that must still be selectable.
tools.notes: See also fillOpacity, textOpacity and opacity.

tools.name: dashed (style key)
tools.description: Draws the stroke as a dashed line; the dash lengths come from dashPattern (default 3 3 scaled by stroke width). The Format panel's line Pattern dropdown writes dashed=1 with different dashPattern presets (dashed, dotted, long dash, dash-dot).
tools.notes: By default the pattern is multiplied by strokeWidth; set fixDash=1 to keep the dash lengths constant.

tools.name: dashPattern (style key)
tools.description: Space-separated list of alternating dash and gap lengths used when dashed=1. Presets used by the Format panel are '1 1' (dotted), '1 2', '1 4', '3 3' (default), '8 8' (long dash) and '10 5 1 5' (dash-dot style patterns). Any even or odd-length list is allowed and repeats along the stroke.

parameters.name: dashPattern
parameters.description: Dash/gap lengths in pixels (multiplied by strokeWidth unless fixDash=1).

tools.notes: Ignored unless dashed=1. Custom stencils use the lowercase <dashpattern> element for the same purpose.

tools.name: fixDash (style key)
tools.description: Keeps the dash pattern in absolute pixels instead of scaling it with strokeWidth. Set it when thick dashed lines produce dashes that are too long, or when several strokes of different widths must share one visual pattern.
tools.notes: Only affects dashed strokes.

tools.name: opacity (style key)
tools.description: Overall opacity of the cell (fill, stroke, image and text) from 0 to 100. This is the Opacity slider in the Format panel Style tab. It is also the property that custom-link setOpacity/fadeTo actions animate at run time.
tools.notes: For finer control use fillOpacity, strokeOpacity and textOpacity separately. Opacity is preserved in SVG/PNG export.

tools.name: shadow (style key)
tools.description: Draws a drop shadow under the shape or edge. The Format panel Shadow checkbox writes shadow=1 per cell; the Diagram tab's Shadow option instead sets the shadow attribute on mxGraphModel for the whole page. Shadow colour, offset, blur and opacity are global and configurable with the shadowColor, shadowOffsetX/Y, shadowBlur and shadowOpacity configuration keys.
tools.notes: In custom stencils the shadow is derived from the <background> element. Transparent PNG exports keep the shadow; some SVG viewers ignore the filter.

tools.name: glass (style key)
tools.description: Adds a glossy highlight over the upper half of the shape, an effect used by the older icon styles. The Format panel exposes it as the Glass checkbox; it is purely decorative and has no effect on edges.
tools.notes: Rendered as a semi-transparent white overlay; it looks best on saturated fills.

tools.name: sketch (style key)
tools.description: Renders the cell with the hand-drawn 'rough' look (jittered outlines, hachure fill). sketch=1 is set per cell by the Format panel Sketch checkbox, by the Sketch theme (ui=sketch) for all new cells, or through Extras > Sketch style. Tuning keys read by the renderer are sketchStyle (rough or comic), fillStyle (hachure, solid, zigzag, cross-hatch, dots, dashed, zigzag-line), fillWeight, hachureGap, hachureAngle, jiggle, curveFitting, disableMultiStroke and disableMultiStrokeFill.

parameters.name: fillStyle
parameters.description: Fill hatching pattern; default hachure for rough style.

parameters.name: hachureGap / hachureAngle / fillWeight
parameters.description: Spacing, angle and line weight of the hatching.

parameters.name: jiggle / curveFitting
parameters.description: Amount of randomness in the outline.

parameters.name: disableMultiStroke / disableMultiStrokeFill
parameters.description: 1 draws a single stroke instead of two overlapping strokes.

tools.notes: Rough rendering is deterministic per cell so exports are stable. The URL parameter rough=0 turns it off for the whole session; sketch=0 on a cell overrides the theme default.

tools.name: comic (style key)
tools.description: Legacy hand-drawn style that perturbs outlines with a fixed wobble but keeps solid fills; it predates sketch=1 and is still written by the Comic checkbox in some themes. Prefer sketch=1;sketchStyle=comic for new diagrams.
tools.notes: comic and sketch can be combined but sketch takes precedence for fills.

tools.name: aspect (style key)
tools.description: aspect=fixed locks the width/height ratio of a vertex so resizing keeps its proportions, which is how icon libraries (AWS, Azure, Cisco) keep logos undistorted. It corresponds to the Constrain Proportions checkbox in the Format panel Arrange tab.

parameters.name: fixed
parameters.description: Lock the aspect ratio during interactive resize.

tools.notes: Only affects interactive resizing; programmatic mxGeometry changes are not constrained. Shift+resize temporarily constrains any shape.

tools.name: rotation (style key)
tools.description: Rotates a vertex (and its label unless horizontal=0/labels are detached) by the given angle in degrees, clockwise. The Format panel Arrange tab's Angle field and the rotation handle write it; Arrange > Direction > Rotate 90 (Ctrl+R) adds 90.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: Angle in degrees, clockwise, default 0; negative values allowed.

tools.notes: Rotated cells keep their unrotated mxGeometry; the bounding box shown on export is the rotated one. rotatable=0 hides the handle.

tools.name: flipH / flipV (style keys)
tools.description: Mirror a vertex horizontally (flipH=1) or vertically (flipV=1) without changing its geometry, so that asymmetric stencils such as arrows, people or valves point the other way. Written by Arrange > Direction > Flip Horizontal / Flip Vertical and the Format panel Arrange tab.
tools.notes: Labels are not mirrored. Stencils that draw text handle flips themselves; custom stencils can use stencilFlipH/stencilFlipV for the same effect.

tools.name: direction (style key)
tools.description: Orientation of directional shapes (triangles, arrows, callouts, cylinders, many stencils and the swimlane header) without rotating the label. Values are east (default), west, north and south. Arrange > Direction > Rotate 90 cycles this key on shapes that support it instead of using rotation.
tools.notes: Some stencils ignore direction and use flipH/flipV or a custom key instead. horizontal=0 rotates the label 90 degrees and is used for vertical swimlanes.

tools.name: perimeter (style key)
tools.description: Chooses the function that computes where edges touch the shape boundary. Built-in perimeters are rectanglePerimeter (default), ellipsePerimeter, rhombusPerimeter, trianglePerimeter, hexagonPerimeter, calloutPerimeter, backbonePerimeter, lifelinePerimeter and the stencil-specific ones registered by libraries. Set perimeter=none to make edges end at the geometric centre.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: rectanglePerimeter, ellipsePerimeter, rhombusPerimeter, trianglePerimeter, hexagonPerimeter, calloutPerimeter, backbonePerimeter, lifelinePerimeter, or none.

tools.notes: Fixed connection points (points=[...] or exitX/exitY) bypass the perimeter unless exitPerimeter/entryPerimeter=1 project them back onto it.

tools.name: perimeterSpacing (style key)
tools.description: Distance in pixels between the shape perimeter and the point where connected edges end, effectively a gap around the shape. On an edge, sourcePerimeterSpacing and targetPerimeterSpacing apply the same idea to each end. Useful when arrowheads must not touch the shape border.
tools.notes: Ignored for edges terminating at fixed connection points.

tools.name: fontColor (style key)
tools.description: Colour of the label text. Accepts a hex colour or default (theme text colour, which flips automatically in dark mode). For HTML labels, inline <font color> or style attributes inside the value override this key for parts of the text.
tools.notes: Set through the Font colour control in the Format panel Text tab. Edge labels use fontColor too, with labelBackgroundColor for the backing box.

tools.name: fontSize (style key)
tools.description: Label font size in pixels (draw.io shows it in pt in the Text tab; the stored value is px, default 12). Ctrl+Shift+Plus / Ctrl+Shift+Minus change it in steps, and autosize=1 or Ctrl+Shift+Y grows the shape to fit.
tools.notes: Inline HTML <font style="font-size:..."> inside the label overrides the key for a span of text.

tools.name: fontFamily (style key)
tools.description: Typeface of the label, default Helvetica. Any font installed on the viewer's machine or supplied as a web font can be named; the Format panel lists defaultFonts from the configuration plus Custom... which lets you enter a Google Fonts name or a font URL. A web font URL is stored in the companion key fontSource (URL-encoded) so exports can embed it.

parameters.name: fontFamily
parameters.description: Font family name, e.g. Helvetica, Verdana, Courier New, Inter.

parameters.name: fontSource
parameters.description: Optional URL-encoded URL of the web font CSS or file used for SVG/PNG embedding.

tools.notes: Fonts are not embedded in PNG exports; the desktop app rasterises with the fonts installed locally. Use the configuration keys defaultFonts, customFonts and fontCss to make fonts selectable for everyone.

tools.name: fontStyle (style key)
tools.description: Bit mask of label text styles: 1 bold, 2 italic, 4 underline (and 8 strikethrough in current versions), summed to combine. Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I / Ctrl+U toggle the bits when a whole cell is selected; inside the rich-text editor the same shortcuts insert inline HTML instead.
tools.usage: fontStyle=<bitmask>;  (1 bold, 2 italic, 4 underline; e.g. 3 = bold italic, 5 = bold underline)
tools.notes: Custom stencils use the same bit values in their <fontstyle> element.

tools.name: align (style key)
tools.description: Horizontal alignment of the label text inside its bounds: left, center (default) or right. Combined with labelPosition it also decides on which side of the shape an outside label sits.
tools.notes: For HTML labels with mixed alignment use inline <div style="text-align:..."> inside the value.

tools.name: verticalAlign (style key)
tools.description: Vertical alignment of the label inside its bounds: top, middle (default) or bottom. Swimlanes and containers typically use verticalAlign=top so the title stays in the header; verticalLabelPosition moves the whole label outside the shape.
tools.notes: Often paired with spacingTop/spacingBottom to fine-tune the offset.

tools.name: labelPosition / verticalLabelPosition (style keys)
tools.description: Place the label outside the vertex bounds: labelPosition=left|center|right shifts the label box horizontally and verticalLabelPosition=top|middle|bottom vertically. The icon libraries use verticalLabelPosition=bottom;verticalAlign=top so captions sit under the icon. The Text tab's Position dropdown (Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Top Left, ...) writes these two keys together with align/verticalAlign.

parameters.name: labelPosition
parameters.description: Horizontal placement of the label box relative to the shape; default center.

tools.notes: For a label to the right of a shape use labelPosition=right;align=left. The label box keeps the shape's width unless labelWidth is set.

tools.name: spacing, spacingTop, spacingBottom, spacingLeft, spacingRight (style keys)
tools.description: Padding in pixels between the label text and the cell bounds. spacing sets all four sides (default 2); the directional keys add to it on one side and can be negative to pull text outward. The Format panel Text tab's Spacing section (Global, Top, Bottom, Left, Right) edits these.
tools.notes: Swimlane headers ignore spacing on the body side. Edge labels honour spacing too, which is handy for moving a label off the line.

tools.name: labelBackgroundColor, labelBorderColor, labelPadding (style keys)
tools.description: Draw a filled and/or bordered box behind the label text, mostly used for edge labels so they remain readable over lines (the default edge style sets labelBackgroundColor to the page background). labelPadding adds pixels around the text inside that box. The Text tab exposes Background and Border colour controls for these.

parameters.name: labelBackgroundColor
parameters.description: Fill behind the label; default (adaptive page colour) or none.

tools.notes: Set labelBackgroundColor=none for transparent edge labels. For vertices the box is drawn only when the label is positioned outside the shape.

tools.name: textOpacity (style key)
tools.description: Opacity of the label text only (0-100), independent of fill and stroke. The Text tab's Opacity field writes it. Use it to dim secondary captions or watermarks without affecting the shape.
tools.notes: Combine with fontColor for tinted transparent text.

tools.name: textDirection (style key)
tools.description: Writing direction of the label for bidirectional scripts: ltr, rtl, or auto (detect from the first strong character), also selectable as Text Direction in the Format panel Text tab. Vertical text is a separate feature (horizontal=0 rotates the label 90 degrees).
tools.notes: Requires html=1 for correct rendering of mixed-direction text.

tools.name: overflow (style key)
tools.description: What happens when the label does not fit the vertex: visible (default, text spills out), hidden (clipped to the bounds), fill (label box stretched to the whole shape, used by table cells), width (label may exceed the height but is clipped to the width) or block (HTML block layout). The Text tab shows it as the Overflow dropdown next to Word Wrap.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Label area equals the shape area (tables, lists).

parameters.name: block
parameters.description: Block-level HTML layout with full width.

tools.notes: labelWidth=<px> fixes the label box width independently of the shape and is useful together with overflow=width.

tools.name: noLabel (style key)
tools.description: Suppresses rendering and editing of the cell's label while keeping the value in the model, for instance on composite parts, icons whose caption lives in a sibling text cell, or edges whose text is carried by separate edge-label children. Double-click still selects the cell but does not open the editor.
tools.notes: Placeholders inside a hidden label are still resolved for tooltips. Compare with editable=0, which shows but locks the label.
